svg.title: The 117 central declarations and the grammar’s laws
svg.desc: Each square is one central declaration, a Lean statement that a row of the coverage file names as central (its 17 rows, phases, differentiations and domains, list 126 central rows, nine declarations twice, so 117 distinct), placed against the edge of one root, how far the one root reaches (08 §7). 11 are read as cases of grammar laws and 1 as a root form at one step, under a stated hypothesis; the rest are counting, below the grammar, or stand at a named distance, each with its reason.
svg.text: The 117 central declarations and the grammar’s laws
Each square is one central declaration, a Lean statement that a row of the coverage file names as
central (its 17 rows, phases, differentiations and domains, list 126 central rows, nine declarations
twice, so 117 distinct), placed against the edge of one root, how far the one root reaches (08 §7). 11
are read as cases of grammar laws and 1 as a root form at one step, under a stated hypothesis; the rest
are counting, below the grammar, or stand at a named distance, each with its reason.
11 derived
each a case of grammar laws, through bridges checked in Lean as equivalences and
support the review reads where a row has them; the case rests on those reviews,
each AI-written
For example, Flow.beyond_gives_nothing: A formation beyond the closure that takes
part at a step gives nothing at that step to a condition a member of the closure
then requires (the closure: a formation's feeding closure)
1 under a stated hypothesis
the root form RootForms.outside_leaves_no_offspring at one step
It is GroupEnding.Flow.all_end: Where every member of a generation is not active,
as where every group depends on one condition that ran into joint excess, the next
generation is empty
6 counting
below the grammar
For example, RelativePosition.rise_needs_fall, in its record's law: No change
raises every part's position, and a part's rise needs another part's fall
99 at a named distance, each with its reason
22 connected
reaching grammar laws without being declared a case of one
32 with balance in their statements
For example, Flow.no_new_dependence: Under balance and inheritance descent forms
no new dependence
18 on amounts
16 at a represented model
representations and not derivations
6 on their own carrier
2 laws of their models
3 keeping significance free
as chapter 7 intends
A named distance says why a declaration is not read as a case of grammar laws; the edge record does not show
that a distance is a gap or a failure. The hypotheses ranking results take, the continuation condition and the
requirement on an order each takes (in many, C; in the direction's, J1 and J2; in others, self-concern), are not
among these: none stands on the edge.
Each declaration's place is in the edge record, one-root-to-its-edge: 42 have a basis in words, in its data, and
the other 75 the label a rule gives; the page of each record whose laws name a declaration prints its place,
with what it rests on. 08 §7's table of places gives no reason for the classes with balance in their statements
(it gives an example), on amounts and laws of their models, and places the 16 at a represented model and the 6
on their own carrier by F5's verified items: theorems, each carried by a law, that state a row of that law's
record at a represented model or on the row's own carrier; shared_laws.py verifies what the Lean can show, and
that a theorem states its row is a reader's judgment. The terms edge of one root, derived and named distance are
in GLOSSARY.md.
Generated by tools/research/spine.py from shared-laws.json and spine.json.
